profile.reading:
DataBank DEN2 sits at 6900 South Peoria Street, Centennial, Colorado; this record's own OpenStreetMap address tag (6900 South Peoria Street, Centennial, CO 80112) matches DataBank's published DEN2 address exactly, confirming the identification despite the OSM record's "zColo by Zayo" name tag. DataBank's own facility page states 31,510 square feet of IT space and 4 megawatts of critical IT load, with 10 to 12 onsite network carriers depending on the page consulted, an N+1 power and cooling design, and FISMA, SOC 1/2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 compliance certifications. DEN2 is one of two buildings on DataBank's Centennial campus, alongside DEN5 at 6961 South Quentin Street; together the two-building, 11-acre campus totals roughly 87,510 square feet and 20 megawatts of combined critical IT load, powered by an off-site Xcel Energy substation per DataBank's own materials. The "zColo by Zayo" name in this record reflects DataBank's December 2020 acquisition of Zayo Group's zColo colocation business, a deal that added 44 data centers and expanded DataBank from roughly 20 to more than 65 facilities across markets including Denver; DataBank's company-history page confirms Denver was among the markets gained through that acquisition, though its current site does not specifically state that 6900 South Peoria was itself a former zColo building, so that lineage is plausible given the market-level confirmation and the persistence of the zColo name in third-party mapping data, but not independently verified building-by-building on DataBank's own site.

Centennial sits in the southern Denver metro, part of the Denver Tech Center-adjacent office and light-industrial corridor that has drawn a mix of telecommunications, colocation, and enterprise IT tenants since the 1990s. Xcel Energy's Colorado service territory has periodically flagged large-load interconnection requests, including data centers, as a growing share of its long-range resource planning, though no Xcel filing specifically naming DataBank's Centennial campus was located this session. Colorado does not offer as extensive a data center-specific sales-tax exemption program as neighboring states, making Denver a comparatively enterprise- and cost-of-living-driven market rather than an incentive-driven one relative to Utah, Nevada, or Texas.
profile.research_note: This OSM point is tagged "zColo by Zayo" but could not be matched with certainty to either DEN2 (6900 S Peoria) or DEN5 (6961 S Quentin) specifically; DataBank's site confirms Denver was gained via the Dec 2020 zColo acquisition at the market level only, not per-building. Reading uses DEN2's address as the primary reference pending confirmation of which specific building this OSM point represents.

reading.body:
DataBank's Centennial campus (DEN2) is one of 17 mapped data center facilities in Colorado and one of only three in the state with published power specifications. The state context shows Colorado has 26.35 MW of published IT capacity across all facilities, but this campus's power rating is not included in the provided data, making its rank of 4 by published megawatts impossible to interpret without the actual figure.

The facility was acquired by DataBank in December 2020 from Zayo's zColo portfolio and retains the zColo branding in some records. No certifications, tenant information, cooling specifications, or grid interconnection details are published for this site. The research status is marked exhausted, indicating the operator's public materials contain no additional technical specifications beyond the address and ownership history.

Without published power specifications, cooling approach, or electrical infrastructure details, this campus cannot be assessed for its role in AI scaling. To evaluate whether DEN2 matters to the grid constraint on AI deployment, specifications on IT load capacity and power availability would need to be obtained directly from DataBank's published materials.
